summary:
The Monkey D. Luffy on card number OP13-118 under the Carrying On His Will label sits on a set title that reaches directly into One Piece's central theme. Inherited will - the idea that a person's resolve outlives them and is picked up by whoever comes next - runs through the manga from its earliest arcs, and it is the specific thread that ties Luffy to the people whose ambitions he ends up carrying. Naming a block after that idea and then putting Luffy in its high card slot is not a coincidence of packaging; it is the set stating its subject. Collectors respond to that, and the card is discussed with more attention to narrative than most numbers in the range receive.

### Basic Info
*   **Main subject / card theme:** Monkey D. Luffy, captain of the Straw Hat Pirates
*   **Set or product (catalog label):** 2025 Piece Card Game Carrying On His Will
*   **Card number:** OP13-118
*   **Language version(s):** English catalog entry
*   **Rarity / treatment:** High-slot printing for this label
*   **Set label year:** 2025

### Community Pulse
Two threads dominate. The first is thematic: because the set title invokes inherited will, collectors read the card as part of a story rather than as a product line item, and discussion tends to run into which characters the theme is actually about. That is unusual - most card threads never leave the topic of condition and price - and it gives this printing a slightly different community texture. The second thread is structural, and it is the practical one: OP13-118 exists under more than one catalog label, including an English manga-art parallel, so buyers have to establish which printing a listing describes. Experienced collectors ask for border and foil detail rather than relying on the number. Condition talk is standard for a recent high-slot card: modern Bandai stock grades reasonably well when it has not been handled, so the spread between clean and average copies is driven mostly by how a card was stored after opening.

### Card Fun Facts
*   Inherited will is one of the most persistent themes in One Piece, which makes it a natural title for a late block and an unusually loaded one for a card set.
*   OP13-118 is shared across catalog labels, so the label is doing identification work rather than sitting in the metadata as a formality.
*   Recent-block cards tend to have cleaner surviving populations than early ones simply because they have spent less time in circulation.

### Summary (TLDR)
OP13-118 Luffy sits under the Carrying On His Will label, a title drawn from One Piece's core theme of inherited resolve. It is discussed with more narrative attention than most cards in the range, and its main practical issue is separating this printing from the other labels sharing the same number.
